THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE T.G. SHIVASHANKARE GOWDA
ORAL JUDGMENT

In this appeal, the petitioner has challenged the judgment and award dated 25.01.2016 passed in M.V.C.No.200/2012 by the Additional Senior Civil Judge, Ramanagara ('the Tribunal' for short)
seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Undisputedly, there was an accident on 26.07.2011 at about 9.00 p.m. at Bidadi on B.M. road,
wherein the car bearing No.KA-05-P-8652 dashed against the pedestrian petitioner causing him injuries.

After taking NC: 2024:KHC:32226 treatment at Government Hospital, Bidadi, NIMHANS,
Bengaluru, Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, Meggan Hospital, Shivamogga, City Hospital, Shivamogga,
the petitioner approached the Tribunal for grant of compensation.
The claim was opposed by the Insurance Company.

The Tribunal after considering the evidence and on hearing both the parties,
by impugned judgment and award, awarded the following compensation:
1. Towards pain and agony Rs.15,000/-
2. Loss of amenities Rs.10,000/-
3.

Medical expenses Rs.56,000/-
4. Loss of income during laid up Rs.5,000/-

Rest, nourishment and attendants Rs.1,000/-
charges 6. Conveyance Rs.2,000/-
7. Loss of future income Rs.61,200/-
8. Future medical expenses Rs.5,000/-
Total Rs. 1,55,200
The award of the Tribunal is satisfied by the Insurance Company.
Pleading inadequacy and seeking enhancement of compensation, the petitioner is before this Court.
4. Heard Ms. Deepika K, learned counsel for Sri Ms. Pramoda K, learned counsel for the petitioner and NC: 2024:KHC:32226 Sri P.B. Raju, learned counsel for respondent No.2 Insurance Company.

5. It is contended by learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner has suffered fracture of left femur, he was under hospitalization for seven days, traveled to various hospitals and spent money towards treatment.
He was earning more than Rs.20,000/- per month by doing agriculture.
The Tribunal did not consider the said income.
The medical evidence of P.W.2 doctor proves that he has suffered 18.2% limb disability which is affecting more than 25% of his earning capacity.

The compensation awarded towards future medical expenses, pain and suffering,
amenities and discomfort, loss of income during the laid up period are on the lower side and sought for enhancement.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that the petitioner though suffered fracture of left femur, post treatment he has become normal and he has resumed his work and there is no future loss of earning.
The medical evidence speaks of 18.2% of NC: 2024:KHC:32226 limb disability and the Tribunal has rightly taken 6% of whole body disability.
For future surgery it is estimated of Rs.20,000/- and there is no evidence that the petitioner requires future surgery for removal of implants.

The compensation awarded is proportionate with the nature of injuries and it is not a case for enhancement and sought for dismissal of the appeal.
7.
I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed by learned counsel for both the parties and perused the material on record.

8. The injury certificate at Ex.P.5 and evidence of P.W.2 doctor Sri Raghunath point out that the petitioner has suffered fracture of left shaft of his femur was under Sri Kumar vs Sri Vijaya Adithya on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48084985/

sentences.text: Future surgery costs around Rs.20,000/-.
The medial bills produced amounting to Rs.56,000/- and the same is considered by the Tribunal.
The Tribunal has considered 6% of whole body disability.

The petitioner being an agriculturist, aged about 32 years, NC: 2024:KHC:32226 certainly the injury will affect his future earnings and therefore functional disability has to be taken at 8% instead of 6%.
9.
The accident is of the year 2011.
The petitioner has not produced any evidence to show his income.

Even if he is treated as a person with no proof of income, in the year 2011, such person will earn not less than Rs.6,500/-
per month.
Hence, his notional income is taken at Rs.6,500/- per month.

10. Having suffered the fracture, the petitioner has to be compensated with Rs.30,000/- towards pain and suffering, reimbursement of medical expenses of Rs.56,000/-, loss of amenities and discomfort Rs.30,000/-, loss of income for three months during laid up period Rs.19,500/-
(Rs.6,500/- x 3 months), incidental expenses such as attendant charges, food and nourishment,
travelling expenses Rs.15,000/-, future medical expenses Rs.10,000/- and loss of future earnings Rs.99,840/-
NC: 2024:KHC:32226 (Rs.6,500/- x 12 x 16 x 8%).

The petitioner is entitled to compensation as follows:
1. Towards pain and agony Rs.30,000/-
2. Loss of amenities Rs.30,000/-
3. Medical expenses Rs.56,000/-
4. Loss of income during laid up Rs.19,500/-
period 5. Rest, nourishment and attendants Rs.15,000/-
charges and conveyance 6.

Loss of future income Rs.99,840/-
7.
Future medical expenses Rs.10,000/-

Less compensation Rs.1,55,200/-
 awarded by the Tribunal

Enhanced compensation Rs.1,05,140/-

ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The impugned judgment and award dated 25.01.2016 passed in M.V.C.No.200/2012 is modified.

(iii) The petitioner would be entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,05,140/-
NC: 2024:KHC:32226 together with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till deposit,
excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.10,000/-.
(iv) The Insurance Company shall deposit the compensation with interest within eight weeks from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this judgment.
